key_insight: Centrosymmetric solids can generate dc photocurrents through coupling between light’s electric and magnetic fields, without broken spatial inversion symmetry.
engineering_relevance: The magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect expands candidate materials for light-to-current conversion and could enable electrical readout of altermagnetic order.
method: Relate photocurrents to dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature.
Classify four injection-like and shift-like mechanisms by time-reversal symmetry and light polarization.
Analyze symmetry constraints and predict responses in monolayer Pt₂HgSe₃ and altermagnetic RuF₄.
evidence_signal: The abstract predicts photocurrent densities on the order of 1 mA/m, with RuF₄’s injection-like current reversing when either light helicity or the Néel vector is switched.
watch_item: These are theoretical predictions; the abstract reports neither experimental validation nor solar-cell conversion efficiency.
paper_title: Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids
